units.title: Making Friends
units.intro: Grammar: subject–verb agreement (including neither/nor, either/or, together with) and the other parts of speech: adverbs, conjunctions, interjections, and prepositions of place, time and movement with their partner words.

cards.title: Subject–verb agreement
rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb (*My friend **lives** here*); a plural subject takes a plural verb (*My friends **live** here*).
With **either ... or** and **neither ... nor**, the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject: *Neither the teacher nor the **students are** here.* / *Either the students or the **teacher is** here.*
**Together with, as well as, along with** do not change the subject: *The captain, together with his players, **is** coming.* **Each, every, everyone, nobody** take a singular verb.

examples.text: Neither Ali nor his brothers is at home.
examples.fix: Neither Ali nor his brothers are at home.

examples.text: The headmaster, as well as the teachers, was present.

cards.title: Forms and examples
head: Subject
Verb
Example
rows: Neither he nor his parents agree.
Either the girls or Meron is right.
Ali, together with his friends, is here.

cards.title: Step by step: present simple with he / she / it
cards.problem: Complete: "Every morning, my father ____ (drink) a cup of coffee."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the time words.** *Every morning* = a habit → present simple.
**Step 2: Find the subject.** *my father* = he → add **-s** to the verb.
**Step 3: Answer.** *my father **drinks***.

cards.title: Step by step: present continuous with a group noun
cards.problem: Complete: "Listen! The school choir ____ (sing) the national anthem right now."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the time words.** *Listen!* and *right now* = happening now → present continuous (am/is/are + -ing).
**Step 2: Find the subject.** *The choir* = one group → singular → **is**.
**Step 3: Answer.** *The choir **is singing***.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I ________ the main reason for his sudden decision to leave the scholarship program.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *understand* is a **state verb** (a verb of thinking or feeling, not an action).

**Step 2:** State verbs do not take -ing: ✗ *am understanding*.

**Step 3:** Subject *I* → **understand** (no -s). So the answer is B.

**Tip:** State verbs (know, understand, like, want, believe, own) stay in the simple form: I understand, she knows.

**In Tigrinya:** 'Understand' (ምርዳእ) ሓደ ካብቶም ናይ ኣእምሮ ኩነታት ዝገልጹ ግሶች (state verbs) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቀጻሊ እዋን (continuous form) ክወስድ ኣይኽእልን እዩ። ኣብ ትግርኛ 'ይርድኣኒ ኣሎ' (ቀጻሊ ዝመስል) እንተበልና እኳ፡ ብእንግሊዘኛ ግን ወትሩ 'understand' (Option B) ጥራይ ኢና ክንጽሕፍ ዘለና።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Samson as well as his two best friends _______ going to the library at the moment.
cards.why: When a subject is joined to another noun by phrases like 'as well as', 'along with', or 'together with', the verb agrees with the first subject. Here, 'Samson' is singular, so the verb must be singular ('is' or 'was'). The time marker 'at the moment' indicates the present continuous tense, making 'is' the correct choice.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The police ________ investigating the robbery that occurred near the national bank.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *police* means the police officers – it is always plural in English.

**Step 2:** Plural subject → plural verb: **are** investigating.

**Step 3:** Do not be tricked: *police* has no -s, but it is still plural.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** 'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ክትርእዮ ከለኻ ናይ ነጸላ (singular) ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) ተገይሩ ስለ ዝውሰድ ድሕሪኡ ዝመጽእ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) ክኸውን ኣለዎ።

cards.title: Step by step: "the number of" + singular verb
cards.problem: Complete: "Since the library was repaired, the number of visitors ____ (increase) a lot."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the real subject.** *the number* (of visitors) – one number → singular.
**Step 2: Choose the tense.** *Since…* means from then until now → present perfect.
**Step 3: Put it together.** singular + present perfect → **has increased** (not *have*).
**Remember:** *the number of* + singular verb; *a number of* (= many) + plural verb.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Each of the candidates who applied for the engineering position ________ a written test.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The subject is **Each** (each one) → singular.

**Step 2:** Ignore *of the candidates who applied…* – it only describes *each*.

**Step 3:** Singular → **has to take**.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'Each' (ነፍሲ ወከፍ) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ነጸላ (singular) እዩ። ስለዚ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ነጸላ ግሲ 'has to take' (Option A) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። 'candidates' (ሕጹያት) ዝብል ቃል ብዙሕ ስለ ዝኾነ 'have' ምምራጽ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Step by step: "one of" + singular verb
cards.problem: Complete: "One of the biggest problems for school leavers ____ the cost of university."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the real subject.** *One* (of the problems) → singular.
**Step 2: Cover the middle words.** *One … ____ the cost* → *One **is***.
**Step 3: Do not match the verb with *problems*.** That word is inside the phrase *of the biggest problems*.

cards.title: Step by step: a group noun + singular verb
cards.problem: Complete: "The board of directors, although they had different ideas, ____ finally agreed on the budget."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the real subject.** *The board* – one group → singular.
**Step 2: Cover the extra words.** *of directors* and *although they had different ideas* do not change the subject.
**Step 3: Choose the verb.** *The board **has** finally agreed.*

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the senior researchers ________ present at the emergency project meeting yesterday.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** With *neither … nor*, the verb agrees with the subject **nearest** to it.

**Step 2:** The nearest subject is *the senior researchers* (plural).

**Step 3:** *yesterday* → past → **were**.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብ 'Neither... nor' ክእሰር ከሎ፡ እቲ ግሲ ምስቲ ናብኡ ዝቐረበ ባእታ ይሰማማዕ (Proximity Rule)። እቲ ዝቐረበ ባእታ 'the senior researchers' (ብዙሕ) ስለ ዝኾነን እቲ ግዜ ድማ 'yesterday' (ትማሊ) ስለ ዝኾነን፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'were' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The local police ________ currently searching the forest area for the prisoners who escaped from the regional jail.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *police* is always plural.

**Step 2:** *currently* = now → present → **are** searching.

**Step 3:** *is* and *was* are singular; *were* is past.

**Tip:** Find the real subject (cover phrases like "of the students" or "with his friends") and make the verb agree with it.

**In Tigrinya:** 'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ብቅርጹ ነጸላ ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) እዩ። 'currently' (ኣብዚ እዋን) ዝብል ቃል ድማ ህልው እዋን ስለ ዝሕብር፡ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **Nearer rules** for either/or and neither/nor; **ignore the extra** after together with / as well as.

cards.title: Step by step: Parts of speech (2) – making the verb agree
body: **Step 1:** Find the subject (a noun or pronoun) and decide if it is singular or plural.
**Step 2:** A singular subject in the present simple takes verb + -s: "The girl reads." A plural subject takes the base verb: "The girls read."
**Step 3:** Ignore phrases between the subject and the verb: "The list of names is long."
**Step 4:** Words like everybody, someone, each, nobody are singular: "Everybody has arrived."
**Step 5:** With either…or / neither…nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject; with "together with / as well as" the verb agrees with the first subject.

**Example:** "The teacher, together with her students, (visit/visits) the museum." First subject = the teacher (singular) → visits. "Either the boys or their father (is/are) at home." Nearer subject = father → is.

cards.title: Mnemonic — "One subject, one -s"
body: the -s goes on the noun OR on the verb, not both (the dog barks / the dogs bark).

cards.title: Exam tip
body: Underline the subject and draw an arrow to the verb before choosing – it stops you being misled by the noun closest to the verb.

cards.title: Parts of speech (2): adverbs, conjunctions, prepositions, interjections
rule: An **adverb** tells **how, when or where** something happens. Many adverbs are an adjective + **-ly**: *slow → slowly, careful → carefully, happy → happily*: *The old man walked **slowly** along the street.* Adverbs of time and place: *yesterday, tomorrow, here, there*: *We must come to school **tomorrow**.*
Watch out: the adverb of *good* is **well**: *He speaks English **well***. *fast, hard, early* stay the same: *She works **hard***. (*lately* is not the adverb of *late*; it means *recently*.)
A **conjunction** joins words or sentences: *and, but, or, because, although, when, while, if*: *Suleman works badly **but** he plays games very well.*

A **preposition** is a short word before a noun or a pronoun. It shows **place, time, direction** or another link: *The telephone is **in** the hall.* *The soldier fought **with** great bravery.* The next lesson (6.3) teaches them step by step.
An **interjection** shows a sudden feeling. It usually has **!** after it: *Oh! Wow! Ouch! Hurrah! Whew!*: ***Hurrah!** We have won the match.*
cards.pattern: adverb = how / when / where  ·  conjunction = joins  ·  preposition + noun  ·  interjection + !

cards.title: Step by step: adjective or adverb?
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "She sings beautiful."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the verb.** *sings* is the action.
**Step 2: Which word tells how she sings?** *beautiful*. But *beautiful* is an adjective: it describes a noun (*a beautiful song*).
**Step 3: A word that tells how an action is done must be an adverb** → adjective + -ly → **beautifully**.
**Check:** *She sings beautifully.* ✔ *She has a beautiful voice.* ✔ (adjective + noun)

cards.title: Common mistakes with these word types
head: Wrong
Right
Why
rows: It tells how she sings → adverb (-ly).
The adverb of good is well.
Although I was tired, but I finished.
Although I was tired, I finished.

cards.title: Memory tip: ask what job the word does
body: Names a person, place or thing → **noun**. Describes a noun → **adjective**. Tells how / when / where → **adverb**.
Joins two words or sentences → **conjunction**. Short word before a noun that shows place, time or direction → **preposition**. A sudden feeling with ! → **interjection**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In "She answered the question correctly", what part of speech is "correctly"?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "correctly" tells how she answered.

**Step 2:** Words that describe verbs are adverbs.

**Step 3:** So it is an adverb.

**Tip:** Ask what job the word does: names a thing → noun; describes a noun → adjective; tells how/when/where → adverb; shows place or time before a noun → preposition.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The suffix -ous makes adjectives (famous, dangerous).

**Step 2:** "dangerously" is an adverb, "endanger" a verb, "dangers" a plural noun.

**Step 3:** So: dangerous.

**Tip:** Ask what job the word does: names a thing → noun; describes a noun → adjective; tells how/when/where → adverb; shows place or time before a noun → preposition.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In "We walked across the bridge", which word is a preposition?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** A preposition shows a relationship of place, direction or time between words.

**Step 2:** "across" shows direction in relation to "the bridge".

**Step 3:** The other words are a verb, a noun and a pronoun.

**Tip:** Ask what job the word does: names a thing → noun; describes a noun → adjective; tells how/when/where → adverb; shows place or time before a noun → preposition.

lessons.title: Prepositions: place, time, movement and partner words

cards.title: What is a preposition?
rule: A **preposition** is a short word that comes **before a noun or a pronoun** and shows how it is linked to the rest of the sentence: *The telephone is **in** the hall.* (where?) *We arrived **at** 6 o'clock.* (when?) *She walked **to** the market.* (which direction?)
Common prepositions: *at, in, on, to, from, for, of, with, by, about, after, before, under, over, above, below, between, among, across, along, through, behind, near, off, up*.
**Step 1:** Ask what the preposition must show: **place**, **time**, **movement**, or is it the **partner** of another word (*good **at**, wait **for***)?
**Step 2:** After a preposition use a **noun**, an **object pronoun** (*me, him, her, us, them*) or a verb + **-ing**: *with **me***, *before **leaving***.
**Step 3:** Some verbs need **no** preposition: *discuss the plan, enter the room, reach Keren, go home*.

examples.text: The soldier fought with great bravery.

cards.pattern: preposition + noun / me, him, her… / verb-ing

cards.title: Place: at, on, in
head: Preposition
Use it for
Examples
rows: a **point**: a place where something happens, a building as a meeting place, an address
at the bus stop, at the door, at school, at home, at the market, at 12 Harnet Avenue
a **surface** or a **line**: tables, walls, floors, streets, rivers; buses, trains, planes
on the table, on the wall, on Harnet Avenue, on a chair, on the bus, on page 12
**inside** a space or an **area**: rooms, boxes, towns, countries, the sea; cars and taxis
in the classroom, in the hall, in Keren, in Eritrea, in the Red Sea, in a taxi
arrive **in** a town or country; arrive **at** a building or place. Never *arrive to*.
We arrived in Barentu. We arrived at the station.

cards.title: Place: other prepositions
head: Preposition
Meaning
Example
rows: The bag is **under** the desk. Write your name **below** the title.
There is a clock **above** the board. The plane flew **over** Asmara.
in the middle of **two** people or things
in a **group** of more than two
She was **among** the best students in her class.
at the back of / facing the front of
The garden is **behind** the house. Wait **in front of** the school.
very close, at the side of
on the other side, facing it
The bank is **opposite** the post office.

cards.title: Time: at, on, in (and no preposition)
head: Preposition
Use it for
Examples
rows: at 6 o'clock, at noon, at night, at midnight, at sunrise, at the moment
on Monday, on 24 May, on Independence Day, on my birthday, on Monday morning
longer times: parts of the day, months, seasons, years, centuries
in the morning, in the evening, in May, in the rainy season, in 1991, in the 20th century
before today, tomorrow, yesterday, tonight, and before this / next / last / every
See you **next Monday**. We met **last year**. I read **every evening**.

cards.title: At, on, in: from small to big
body: **TIME:** **at** 7 o'clock (a point) → **on** Monday (a day) → **in** May (a month) → **in** 2026 (a year).
**PLACE:** **at** the door (a point) → **on** the wall (a surface) → **in** the room (a space) → **in** Asmara (an area).
**AT** = a point. **ON** = a surface, a line or a day. **IN** = inside, or a longer time.

cards.title: Movement and direction
head: Preposition
Meaning
Example
rows: We go **to** school by bus. (But: go **home** – no *to*.)
the start and the end of a journey
moving onto a surface / away from it
The cat jumped **onto** the table. He fell **off** his bicycle.
from one side to the other side of a flat thing
in at one end and out at the other
We walked **along** the beach in Massawa.
They climbed **up** the hill and ran **down** the steps.
The ship **made for** (moved towards) the harbour.
Walk **past** the bank and turn left.

cards.title: Words that are easy to mix up
head: Pair
How they are different
Examples
rows: **by** = not later than (a deadline; the action happens once before it). **until** = all the time up to then (the action goes on).
Hand in your homework **by** Friday. / I will wait **until** 5 o'clock.
**for** + a length of time. **since** + the starting point. Both often go with *have/has + 3rd form*.
I have lived here **for** three years. / I have lived here **since** 2023.
**during** the lesson / **while** the teacher was talking
**in** = where something is (no movement). **into** = moving from outside to inside.
She is **in** the room. / She ran **into** the room.
**between** two (or clearly separate) people or things. **among** a group.
**on time** = at the planned time, not late. **in time** = early enough to do something.
The bus left **on time**. / We arrived **in time** to see the start.
**at the end of** + something. **in the end** = finally, after a long time.
**at the end of** the film / **In the end**, he came to the house.
Sit **beside** me. / **Besides** English, she speaks Arabic.

cards.title: Partner prepositions: words that always take the same preposition
head: Word
Preposition
Example
rows: the story / lack / as a result
the story **of** her life; lack **of** food; as a result **of** the rain
pay **for** food; wait **for** the bus; ask **for** money; look **for** my key
I bought this hat **for** fifty-five Nakfa.
thanks **to** the doctor; owe your life **to** me; send the bill **to** him; listen **to** the radio; belong **to** me
I am grateful **to** you **for** your help.
My grandmother **looks after** the baby. (= takes care of)
afraid **of** snakes; proud **of** my country; tired **of** waiting
depend **on** the rain; married **to** Senait; laugh **at** a joke

cards.title: Step by step: textbook exercise (Lesson 6.5 B), sentences 1–8
cards.problem: Put in the correct prepositions. 1. Abraham lived ___ Akurdet ___ great poverty. 2. Zeineb wrote the story ___ her life. 3. Jimie was still ___ need ___ money, and he could not even pay ___ his food. 4. ___ times, as a result ___ his lack ___ food he became ill. 5. He got better, thanks ___ the doctor who looked ___ him. 6. The doctor sent a report ___ his visits. 7. He waited ___ several weeks and then sent the bill ___ him again. 8. ___ the end, he came ___ the house and asked ___ his money.

steps.text: **Step 1: Place or state.** 1. lived **in** Akurdet (a town → in) **in** great poverty (a state → in).
**Step 2: Partner words with "of".** 2. the story **of** her life. 3. **in** need **of** money. 4. as a result **of**, lack **of** food.
**Step 3: Partner words with "for".** 3. pay **for** his food. 7. waited **for** several weeks (a length of time). 8. asked **for** his money.
**Step 4: Fixed phrases.** 4. **At** times (= sometimes). 8. **In** the end (= finally).
**Step 5: "to" for the person who receives, or the place you go.** 5. thanks **to** the doctor. 7. sent the bill **to** him. 8. came **to** the house.
**Step 6: Other partners.** 5. looked **after** him (= took care of him). 6. a report **on** his visits (*of* is also possible).

cards.answer: 1. in, in  2. of  3. in, of, for  4. At, of, of  5. to, after  6. on (of)  7. for, to  8. In, to, for

cards.title: Step by step: textbook exercise (Lesson 6.5 B), sentences 9–15
cards.problem: 9. I expected gratitude ___ you, as you owe your life ___ me. 10. I am not ungrateful ___ you ___ what you did, so I will give my life ___ you. 11. He is sitting ___ a chair and looking ___ ___ the window. 12. The ship made ___ the harbour. 13. We arrived ___ Barentu ___ exactly 6 o'clock. 14. I bought this hat ___ fifty-five Nakfa. 15. I have been waiting ___ over an hour and a half.

steps.text: **Step 1: Who gives and who receives?** 9. gratitude **from** you (you give it); owe your life **to** me (I receive it). 10. (un)grateful **to** a person **for** a thing; give my life **for** you (= to help you).
**Step 2: Place and movement.** 11. sitting **on** a chair (a surface); looking **out of** the window (from inside to outside). 12. made **for** the harbour (= moved towards it).
**Step 3: Place and time together.** 13. arrived **in** Barentu (a town → in) **at** exactly 6 o'clock (a clock time → at).
**Step 4: Price.** 14. bought **for** fifty-five Nakfa.
**Step 5: Length of time.** 15. *over an hour and a half* is a length → **for** (not *since*).

cards.answer: 9. from, to  10. to, for, for  11. on, out of  12. for  13. in, at  14. for  15. for

cards.title: Common mistakes
head: Wrong
Right
Why
rows: No preposition before next / last / this / every.
We arrived to Barentu at the evening.
We arrived in Barentu in the evening.
arrive in + town; in the evening.
He entered the room. / He went into the room.
I have lived here since three years.
I have lived here for three years.
During I was eating, the phone rang.
While I was eating, the phone rang.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Barentu is a town → arrive **in**.

**Step 2:** 6 o'clock is a clock time → **at**.

**Step 3:** *arrive to* is never correct; *on* is for days and dates.

**Tip:** Time: at + clock time, on + day/date, in + month/year/part of the day. Place: at a point, on a surface or a line, in a space or an area. Length of time → for; starting point → since; deadline → by; all the time up to then → until; during + noun, while + subject + verb.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Please hand in your essays ____ Friday. Late essays will not be marked.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Friday is the **last** day: a deadline.

**Step 2:** Deadline (not later than) → **by**.

**Step 3:** *until* would mean you keep handing in the essay all the time up to Friday – wrong meaning.

**Tip:** Time: at + clock time, on + day/date, in + month/year/part of the day. Place: at a point, on a surface or a line, in a space or an area. Length of time → for; starting point → since; deadline → by; all the time up to then → until; during + noun, while + subject + verb.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *the meeting* is a noun, not subject + verb.

**Step 2:** during + noun → **during** the meeting.

**Step 3:** *while* needs subject + verb: *while we were meeting*.

**Tip:** Time: at + clock time, on + day/date, in + month/year/part of the day. Place: at a point, on a surface or a line, in a space or an area. Length of time → for; starting point → since; deadline → by; all the time up to then → until; during + noun, while + subject + verb.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: He walked ____ the classroom and sat down at his desk.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** He moved from **outside** to **inside**.

**Step 2:** Movement to the inside → **into**.

**Step 3:** *walked in the classroom* means he walked around inside it – not the meaning here.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Singular subjects take singular verbs and plural subjects plural verbs; with either/or and neither/nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Adverbs tell how, when or where (often -ly); conjunctions join; interjections show feelings with !. Prepositions come before a noun or pronoun: at a point / on a surface or day / in a space or longer time; for + length, since + start, by = deadline, until = up to then, during + noun, while + subject + verb; and many words have a partner preposition (good at, wait for, look after).

glossary.meaning: The verb matches the subject in number.
A word that describes a verb, adjective or adverb.
A short word before a noun or pronoun that shows place, time, direction or another link: in, on, at, to, for, since, by, with.

tips.text: **Nearer rules** for either/or and neither/nor; **ignore the extra** after together with / as well as.
**AT** a point, **ON** a surface or a day, **IN** a space or a longer time.
